human_tolerance.notes: A bird of open, dry country with scattered shrub and tree cover, which the article lists as savanna and farmland, so it uses open suburban ground rather than a built-up core.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Seasonal breeders with a summer peak: in summer the testes can weigh up to 1.6 g and in winter no breeding activity takes place. The female incubates 6 to 12 eggs for 26 to 28 days.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Outside the breeding season the birds forage on grain, tubers and seed, including agricultural crop spillage; males still spar aggressively.

vocalizations.description: A harsh, grating rattling call given by both sexes, used to keep the flock together and in male sparring; the article also records a gaping beak as part of a male's display.

external.note: GBIF usageKey 2473341 from the species/match endpoint and iNaturalist taxon 1428 from the taxa endpoint; the Wikidata QID is the one the English article's taxobox links to.

conservation.note: The species article's taxobox records IUCN category Least Concern.

range.note: The article says only that the species 'is native to Africa, mainly south of the Sahara', with no country list, so only ZA is recorded rather than inventing a country set. Introduced populations are recorded for the three introduced countries the article names directly, Australia, Brazil and North America (recorded as US); the West Indies and Colombia are named but are not single ISO 3166-1 codes and are left in the note.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: AVONET gives Primary.Lifestyle Terrestrial for this species, and the article records that keets 'can flutter onto low branches' thanks to rapid wing growth, which together give Walk and Fly.

traits.flight.note: The article records flight in the form of the keets fluttering onto low branches a week after hatching and of the males raising their wings in display.

traits.nest_type.note: 'The nest is a well-hidden, generally unlined scrape'.

traits.perching.note: Recorded from the young fluttering onto low branches and from the male display in which the wings are raised, which is perching-class behaviour in a mostly terrestrial bird.

traits.mass_kg.note: AVONET Mass 1299 g, sourced by AVONET to Dunning; the species article independently gives 1.3 kg, which agrees.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: The article's single figure of 1.3 kg is treated as the upper end of the bracket and 1.2 kg is authored as the lower bound, since no mass range is published in the cited sources.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Twice the AVONET Wing.Length of 253.8 mm, rounded to 0.508 m. AVONET does not give a wingspan directly.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Honest gap. Neither the species article, Wikidata nor GBIF gives a wild longevity figure for this species, and no openly licensed source with one was found. 12 years is an authored placeholder for a galliform; it is not a sourced value.

traits.diet.note: 'During the nonbreeding season, N. meleagris consumes corns, tubers, and seeds, particularly of agricultural weeds, as well as various agricultural crop spillage. During the breeding season, more than 80% of their diet may be invertebrates, particularly arthropods such as beetles.' The record splits the year-round diet as 0.5 invertebrate / 0.4 seed / 0.1 fruit, which is an authored average of the two stated seasonal regimes rather than a figure the source gives.

traits.senses.note: Authored: diurnal galliform with coloured vision and modest olfaction.

traits.social.note: Authored. The article does not give a flock size; it records that more than one hen may use a nest, implying hens group, and that males spar and defend by display. Group with a 2 to 20 bracket is a judgement.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Recorded as diurnal: a daytime ground forager with no nocturnal behaviour described.

traits.defense.note: Mob. 'Males often show aggression towards each other, and partake in aggressive fighting, which may leave other males bloodied and otherwise injured', using raised wings, bristled feathers and a gaping beak.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement from a bird that habitually feeds on agricultural crop spillage, which puts it close to people and accustomed to open, disturbed ground.

habitat.use.note: AVONET gives Primary.Lifestyle Terrestrial and Habitat Woodland for this species, and the article says the bird 'breed in warm, fairly dry and open habitats with scattered shrubs and trees such as savanna or farmland' and 'scratch in loose soil for food'. The 0.8 ground / 0.2 arboreal split is authored from that.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Authored from the 'scattered shrubs and trees' habitat and the keets' use of low branches: rests up on branches.

habitat.resources.note: The three food tags map onto the two seasonal diet sentences in the article, and nest_ground follows the 'unlined scrape' nest. Weights are authored.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Adapter is authored from the farmland and open-habitat preference the article gives; dist_building_min_m, light_max and road_mortality are authored judgements.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'Helmeted guinea fowl are seasonal breeders ... during winter no breeding activity takes place' describes the reproductive cycle, not dormancy of the whole bird, so ActiveYearRound is recorded.

seasonal.phases.note: The summer breeding peak and winter non-breeding season are stated in the source. The calendar months attached to them, November to March and April to October, are authored, because the source describes them relative to summer and winter rather than by date.

seasonal.life_stages.note: A clutch of 6 to 12 eggs incubated for 26 to 28 days gives the 27-day egg stage. The 30-day juvenile duration and 0.6 scale are authored; the source says the keets can flutter onto low branches within about a week of hatching but gives no fledging date.

vocalizations.song.note: The article describes the gaping beak of a displaying male but does not transcribe the call, so this description of a harsh grating rattling call is authored and flagged as a judgement rather than a sourced transcription.

look.note: Authored, and explicitly a judgement rather than a sourced description: the article discusses the casque and the wattles but gives no full plumage description, so the colours here follow the well-known appearance of the species - a slate-grey body with fine white spotting, a bare bluish head with red wattles and a bony casque on the crown. Proportions are authored. A reviewer wanting a sourced description should replace this block.

behavior.note: Mostly authored for the shared ground-forager program, which the article's behaviour supports: a bird that walks and scratches loose soil for invertebrates and seed, flushes into flight when threatened, and is active in daylight. flee_gait fly and the daylight rest window are authored from that. The shared program is not mammal-specific in its logic, and a reptile record in this repository already uses it.
